result.summary: Switches the mining block template manager's WaitAndCreateNewBlock loop from NodeClock to SteadyClock for timeout and fee polling tick measurements. NodeClock is retained strictly for checking the testnet 20-minute minimum difficulty rule against tip timestamps, and header documentation is added explaining the 20-minute difficulty constraint.
result.problem: WaitAndCreateNewBlock previously measured its overall timeout and 1-second fee polling interval using the wall clock (NodeClock). System wall clock adjustments could artificially lengthen or shorten wait durations, and frozen mocktime during testing prevented the wait from ever timing out.
evidence: Commit 15186686ac: 'waitNext measures its timeout and 1-second fee tick with the wall clock, while waitTipChanged uses the steady clock. This means a wall clock jump changes how long waitNext waits, and it never times out while mocktime is frozen.'
result.changed_since_previous: Added commit cac1ef8cdb, which adds doc comments to interfaces/mining.h explaining the strict 20-minute testnet minimum-difficulty rule for block headers, and adjusted the testnet check condition to require strictly more than 20 minutes (NodeClock::now() >= tip_time + 20min + 1s). The previous dependency #36862 has now merged.
result.card: This PR switches BlockTemplateManager::WaitAndCreateNewBlock to use SteadyClock instead of NodeClock for its loop deadline and fee tick. Using wall clock time previously caused template wait timeouts to fluctuate during system clock adjustments and prevented timeouts entirely when mocktime was frozen in tests. NodeClock is retained exclusively for testnet 20-minute minimum difficulty block template triggers, which is also documented in the mining interface.

risk.why: Touches internal mining template waiting timeouts and testnet difficulty template generation logic; a bug could cause WaitAndCreateNewBlock to time out early, hang, or miscalculate testnet minimum-difficulty block timings.
